A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SecA is a universal protein translocase that is present in all organisms, from the cyanobacter to humans.
the SecA protein is an evolutionarily conserved protein that is involved in protein translocation in all three domains of life.
the SecA protein is an essential factor in the translocation of both cytoplasmic- and thylakoidal-type membrane proteins in cyanobacterial photosynthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cyanobacterial genome contains genes for the Sec protein translocase system, which mediates translocation of proteins across both membranes in the cell.
the SecA protein, a key protein in the translocation machinery, is conserved among cyanobacteria, eubacteria, algae, and higher plants.
SecA proteins in cyanobacteria are involved in translocation of proteins across the cytoplamic and thylakoidal membranes.
